title: Connexions projectives et uniformisation : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (from the previous page). X/S is a relative curve and Ω is a line bundle, in effect the conormal/cotangent line. Ŝ = Sym^∧(Ω) is the completed symmetric algebra, an augmented algebra with augmentation ideal J. A 'connection' on Ŝ is a map C: Ŝ → Ŝ ⊗̂ Ω^1_{X/S} satisfying Leibniz. It is determined by its value on a local generator ω_0 of Ω: C(ω_0) = Σ_{i≥0} ω_0^i ⊗ ϖ_i. The coefficient ϖ_0 ∈ Ω^1_{X/S} ⊗ Ω^{-1} is the 'Kodaira–Spencer' or transversality term and is assumed invertible. In modern terms this is a Grothendieck connection (stratification) on a formal line bundle over X, a formal model of the neighbourhood of a section in a P^1-bundle. A connection c on a P^1-bundle P (projective connection, or a connection on the corresponding rank-3 Lie algebra of type sl_2) induces on the formal completion along a transversal section a connection ĉ of 'Riccati form': C(ω_0) = ϖ_0 + ω_0 ϖ_1 + ω_0^2 ϖ_2, with no terms of degree ≥ 3.

Computation on this page. Change the formal coordinate by an automorphism u of the augmented algebra Ŝ, ω_0 ↦ ω_0(1 + Σ α_i ω_0^i). Grothendieck writes the transformed connection as (ϖ_0 + ω̃ϖ_1 + ω̃^2 ϖ_2)·[1 + Σ(i+1) α_i ω̃^i] plus terms in ω̃^{·} ⊗ dα_i.
- Assume α_2 = 0 and work mod J^4. The result is C(ω_0) + 4α_3 ω_0^3 ϖ_0. A degree-3 term is forbidden in Riccati form, so α_3 = 0.
- Inductively, if α_2 = α_3 = … = α_{k-1} = 0, then mod J^{k+1} the new term is (k+1) α_k ω_0^k ϖ_0. Hence (k+1) α_k = 0.
- Mod J^3 one finds instead C(ω_0) + 3α_2 ω_0^2 ϖ_0. This is still of Riccati form: α_2 merely shifts ϖ_2 by 3α_2 ϖ_0. This is the affine action of quadratic differentials (Γ(Ω^{⊗2}) up to twist) on projective connections.

Proposition. Let Conn(P) be the projective connections on P (equivalently, on the Lie algebra of P). Let G_0 be the group of automorphisms of the augmented algebra Ŝ that are the identity mod J^4. Then Conn(P) × G_0 → Conn(Ŝ), (c,u) ↦ u(ĉ), is bijective. Grothendieck's justification is 'car … 0', i.e. it uses characteristic 0 so that the integers k+1 are invertible.

Next page. Let G be the automorphisms that are the identity mod m^3, so G/G_0 ≅ Γ(Ω^{⊗2}). He shows G_0 × G(c) → G is bijective, where G(c) is the set of h with hĉ again of Riccati form.

Purpose. Every formal connection on the formal line (a formal 'coordinate system' along the diagonal) can be normalized uniquely by a coordinate change tangent to the identity to order 3 into Riccati form. Thus projective connections are exactly formal connections modulo the 'non-Möbius' part of Aut(Ŝ). This is the formal-geometric content of 'projective structure = 3-jet of a coordinate modulo PGL_2', and the algebraic shadow of the Schwarzian derivative, serving a uniformisation programme.
errors: Transformation formula: a correct coordinate change should divide by f'(ω̃)=1+Σ(i+1)α_iω̃^i (or substitute the inverse series), not multiply by it. The sign and leading coefficient of the obstruction term may therefore be off. The conclusion (k+1)α_k=0 is unaffected at leading order.
Exponent of the dα_i terms: for f(ω)=ω(1+Σα_iω^i) the dα_i term should carry ω^{i+1}, not ω^{i+2}, consistent with the factor (i+1)α_iω^i.

The induction tacitly assumes ϖ_0 invertible (transversality of the section) and k+1 invertible in O_S. In characteristic p the step k=p-1 gives no constraint. The coefficient 3α_2 also degenerates in characteristic 3. So the Proposition as stated needs characteristic 0 (or residue characteristic large relative to the truncation). Grothendieck's parenthetical seems to acknowledge this.
Mixed indices: 'n' versus 'k' in the inductive step.

ideas.what: Normalization of a formal connection on Sym^∧(Ω) to Riccati (degree ≤2) form by an automorphism tangent to identity to order 3, with uniqueness
ideas.modern_name: Projective structures as formal coordinates modulo PGL_2 / Aut O ⊃ Aut_+ O reduction; opers for sl_2 in formal-coordinate language
ideas.usually_credited_to: Gunning (1960s), Deligne (1970, Équations différentielles à points singuliers réguliers), Beilinson–Drinfeld (opers, formal-coordinate torsors, 1990s)

ideas.what: Affine action of quadratic differentials on projective connections (α_2 shifts ϖ_2 by 3α_2ϖ_0); G/G_0 ≅ Γ(Ω^{⊗2})
ideas.modern_name: Projective connections form a torsor under quadratic differentials (Schwarzian derivative)

ideas.what: Inductive obstruction (k+1)α_k=0 showing dependence on invertibility of integers
ideas.modern_name: Characteristic-p failure of uniqueness of formal coordinate normalizations (related to p-curvature / dormant opers)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Mochizuki (p-adic Teichmüller, indigenous bundles, 1990s); Y. Ihara earlier

missed.claim: Grothendieck develops projective connections and uniformisation in a purely formal-algebraic way: connections on the completed symmetric algebra of the conormal line, with a group-factorization G = G_0 · G(c). He visibly tracks the integer coefficients (k+1) that obstruct the result in positive characteristic. This is an unpublished precursor of the 'formal coordinates / Aut O-torsor' treatment of opers, but the result itself is standard.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Documents Grothendieck's own approach to projective structures, relevant to the history behind Mochizuki's indigenous bundles and Beilinson–Drinfeld opers. No new mathematics for specialists.

deep.surprise_reason: The page is a careful but standard computation: a formal-coordinate normalization of a projective connection to Riccati form, with a uniqueness statement. It is mathematically classical (Gunning/Deligne/opers). Interest is mainly historical: it shows Grothendieck's formal-group-style formulation and his attention to characteristic.
transcription_corrections: 'C(ω_0^~)^{n-1}' is probably C applied to the transformed coordinate (u^{-1} or tilde superscript), not an (n-1)-th power.
Final line likely reads '[Cette application est bijective (si de car. 0)]' or '(car car. 0)', i.e. a characteristic-0 hypothesis.
In the Proposition, 'G_0 le groupe des automorphismes de Ŝ (alg. augmentée) qui induisent l'identité mod 𝔍^4', consistent with the next page's G (identity mod m^3) and G/G_0 ≅ Γ(Ω^{⊗2}).
'Calculons [mod] Ω^3 en supposant …' likely refers to mod J^3 in general (α_2 arbitrary).
